summary: Option A needs explicit separation between dev-flow and dev-loop brief schemas, plus a real process supervisor around the proposed socket bridge. The largest risks are authorization, cancellation semantics, Slack webhook/Socket Mode parity, and assuming the example server wiring can be lifted unchanged.

suggestions.title: Use an explicit topology discriminator
suggestions.rationale: The current CLI parses brief files through dev-loop `parse_brief`, where `kind: feature` means document-based `FeatureBrief`. Dev-flow natural-language intake instead accepts only `enhancement` or `new_feature` through `DevRequestBrief`. A Slack feature request cannot safely reuse the existing `--brief` contract; make `--type bug|feature` select separate parsers and carry `--base` explicitly because `DevRequestBrief` has no base-branch field.

suggestions.title: Extract a package-owned dev-flow builder
suggestions.rationale: `server_dev.py::_on_startup` is not self-contained: it depends on `examples`-only `server.py` helpers, `mcp_wiring`, model-plan defaults, graph memory, Jira/Git/Wiki toolkits, and per-run checkpoint kwargs. Extract a library builder with explicit dependencies and return the exact `dev_loop_flow_kwargs` required by `DevFlowRunner` recovery, then make the example delegate to it.

suggestions.title: Split preflight by topology
suggestions.rationale: The existing CLI preflight only checks that a Redis URL exists, while also hard-failing Jira and worktree checks. The dev-flow example treats Jira as optional and its natural-language brief has different prerequisites from `WorkBrief`. Add topology-specific checks, including an actual Redis connectivity probe, so valid feature requests are not rejected by bug-mode requirements.

suggestions.title: Enforce initiator authorization outside the REST contract
suggestions.rationale: `register_command_routes` is deliberately auth-agnostic, and its handlers trust caller-supplied `resolved_by` and `requested_by`. A Unix socket authenticates the local bot process, not the Slack user, and a restarted bot loses any in-memory ownership map. Persist run ownership in Redis and validate team/channel/user before forwarding commands; use a per-run capability for the child socket so local clients cannot impersonate Slack operators.

suggestions.title: Fix Slack ingress authentication and mode parity first
suggestions.rationale: The webhook interactive route is registered directly to `SlackInteractiveHandler.handle`, which does not verify the Slack signature. Socket Mode slash commands call `_is_authorized(channel)` without passing `user`, bypassing `allowed_user_ids`. New gate actions would otherwise expose resolve/cancel through an unauthenticated webhook or unauthorized Socket Mode user.

suggestions.title: Add a gate-reply interceptor before normal message handling
suggestions.rationale: Current message handling sends text directly to `_safe_answer`; there is no thread-to-run/gate correlation layer. Threaded fallback replies must be intercepted before the agent path, matched by channel and thread timestamp, restricted to the run initiator, and implemented identically for webhook and Socket Mode.

suggestions.title: Make cancellation terminate the child flow
suggestions.rationale: `DevLoopRunner.cancel_run()` only applies `RunCancelled`; it does not cancel the underlying flow task. `SessionHost.wait_gate()` wakes only on gate resolution or expiry, so a parked run can continue waiting after `/cancel`. The headless runtime needs a cancellation hook that records the existing action, cancels the run task, waits for teardown, and escalates to process termination when necessary.

suggestions.title: Specify a bounded subprocess supervisor
suggestions.rationale: The proposed handshake uses stdout, so the parent must continuously drain stdout/stderr or a verbose child can block on a full pipe. The state tail retries Redis failures indefinitely, while exception paths do not emit `run/closed`; therefore the supervisor needs handshake and liveness deadlines, child-exit classification, tail cancellation, SIGTERM/SIGKILL escalation, and deterministic socket cleanup.

suggestions.title: Add integration-level admission control
suggestions.rationale: The runner already uses a semaphore controlled by `FLOW_MAX_CONCURRENT_RUNS`, but one subprocess per Slack request creates one independent runner per process and bypasses any host-wide cap. Treat “unlimited” as an explicit opt-in; otherwise enforce a bounded integration cap with queued/rejected status and cleanup for abandoned requests.

suggestions.title: Extend the Slack wrapper for debounced status updates
suggestions.rationale: The wrapper currently has `_post_message()` but returns no message timestamp and has no `chat.update` abstraction. A status card requires a stable channel/message identifier, one writer per card, retry handling, and debounce/coalescing before Slack Tier 3 limits are reached. Keep Slack API calls in the wrapper rather than the transport-neutral run core.

suggestions.title: Test the real cross-process contract
suggestions.rationale: Existing REST tests exercise an in-process `web.Application`, and stream tests use fake Redis. Add an aiohttp Unix-site/client test covering handshake, `open_questions` answers, first-writer 409, cancel, child crash before terminal action, Redis loss, and socket cleanup; run the same Slack authorization cases through webhook and Socket Mode handlers.

suggestions.title: Declare Redis in the devloop integration extra
suggestions.rationale: `redis>=5.0` is currently listed under the integrations `msteams` and `broadcast` extras, not under `slack`; installing `ai-parrot-integrations[slack]` does not guarantee the dependency needed by the proposed state tail. Add a dedicated devloop extra or make the Slack devloop feature depend on one, and test the documented installation path.
